title: John Philpot Curran
html_source: John Philpot Curran, (born July 24, 1750, Newmarket, County Cork, Ire.—died Oct. 14, 1817, Brompton, Middlesex, Eng.), Irish lawyer and statesman who is remembered as a great advocate and as a champion of Irish liberties. Although handicapped by small stature and a speech impediment, he soon became celebrated for his quick wit and courage in defending apparently hopeless cases. Though not a Roman Catholic himself, he fought in the Irish House of Commons for Roman Catholic emancipation.
